source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: To encourage flowering, this source describes deliberately imposing a period of mild water stress on the tree: irrigation is reduced or withheld for a defined period (commonly at the start of a dry spell in the growing calendar) to signal the tree to shift from vegetative growth into reproductive (flowering) mode, after which irrigation is resumed gradually to support flower development without causing flower drop from too abrupt a change. This technique requires judgment and local experience, since withholding water for too long or too aggressively can stress the tree into leaf drop rather than flowering, while too little water stress may fail to trigger flowering strongly. The exact physiological mechanism by which water stress triggers flowering is described in general terms in the source rather than fully explained mechanistically, so this entry should be read as a practical technique description rather than a complete scientific explanation.
